# dsh-codex-reset-tracker
DeepSeek Harness plugin for Codex reset status. It adds a composer entry with a compact status popov
er and registers the read-only `codex_reset` agent tool.
## Screenshots
| Light theme | Dark theme |
## What it shows
- The composer entry reports the source site's live schedule probability (for example, **≥86% Yes**)
, alongside the latest completed reset and next expected time. The heading switches to an upcoming-r

eset question when a live schedule is available.
- Schedule confidence comes directly from the publi
c API and is rounded to a percent as on the source page. In the popover, a live schedule displays pr
obability + Yes even below 80% or when its local date is tomorrow. A completion reported today takes
priority. Scheduled events remain schedule records and do not replace the latest completed reset. T
he day check uses the browser's local calendar day; completion times prefer `completedAt`, then `eff

ectiveAt`, then `announcedAt`.
- The popover includes the Tibo Sottiaux source post. It shows the Si

mplified Chinese translation and the English source when both differ.
- The dock entry follows the p
opover's schedule rules. When no completion has been reported today and a live pending schedule has
a rounded probability of at least 80%, its label becomes `Codex Reset ≥86%` (`Codex Reset 100%` at 1
00%); otherwise it stays `Codex Reset Tracker`. Only the percentage is violet; the name keeps its no
rmal color. The percentage shares the name's font weight and keeps its violet color on hover and whe
n expanded. Normal refreshes keep the last successful, still-valid forecast visible. A failed reques
t restores the default label until a later successful response confirms a valid forecast. Unread mar
kers and unread storage are removed. The entry reserves the widest label in the active language so n
eighbouring controls stay in place, while the hover background and clickable area fit the visible co

ntent.
- The client requests `/status` on mount and refreshes every 10 minutes. Opening the popover,
returning to the foreground, or reconnecting checks for updates when the snapshot is at least 60 se
conds old. Requests time out after 20 seconds and respect rate-limit cooldowns. The popover displays
the local time zone and fetch time; fetch time is not the upstream monitor time. The agent tool can

query status or paginated records.
- When today's reset answer turns from no to yes, the client rai
ses one system notification saying `Codex has reset` (`Codex 已经重置` in Chinese). Notifications need b
rowser permission: the popover footer offers Enable notifications, and only that click asks for it;
a denial or an unsupported browser simply sends nothing. Recent completion IDs are deduplicated acro
ss status slots and kept in local storage so a reload stays quiet; browsers supporting Web Locks als
o coordinate concurrent pages. Without that coordination, cross-page deduplication is best effort. A
blocked storage API deduplicates only within the current page, and the first load only records a ba
seline instead of replaying history. Detection rides the polling above, so it can lag by up to one r
f replaying history. Detection rides the polling above, so it can lag by up to one refresh interval.

## Agent tool
`codex_reset` supports:

- `action: "status"` — the latest global and Banked reset signals and the next scheduled reset.
- `a
ction: "records"` — one page of records, filtered by `kind`, `page`, and `pageSize`.
The tool accepts an optional `lang` for record translations. Successful responses are cached for 60
optional `lang` for record translations. Successful responses are cached for 60 seconds by default.

| Config | Default | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| `apiBaseUrl` | `https://didcodexreset.com/openapi/v1

` | Public API base URL used by the agent tool |
| `cacheTtlSeconds` | `60` | Tool response cache, f

rom 5 to 3600 seconds |
| `timeoutMs` | `20000` | Tool call timeout, from 1000 to 120000 millisecond

5 to 3600 seconds |
| `timeoutMs` | `20000` | Tool call timeout, from 1000 to 120000 milliseconds |
Override these values under the plugin row's `config` in `cordis.patch.yml`. The public API document
s a shared limit of 60 requests per hour per IP.
